title: The first request: replace the worst transformers

questions.stem: Two transformers both score 95 on condition, cost the same and have the same PoF. One feeds 300 homes; the other feeds a hospital and 5,000 homes. Which does the first lesson's model replace first, and why?

options.text: The 300-home one, since the ranking's tie-break by id is kept
options.says: The model does not use the ranking: it kept only 2 of the 9 ranked units.

options.text: The hospital's, since risk is PoF times what one failure costs
options.says: Right: equal PoF and cost, so the larger consequence of failure decides.

options.text: Either one, since equal scores mean equal risk in the first model
options.says: T00033 and T00076 share a score of 100 and one's failure costs five times the other's.

options.text: The 300-home one, since condition already prices a failure
options.says: Condition says how worn a unit looks; risk also needs what a failure costs.

origin.section: A Condition Score Is Not Risk, and the Ranking Cannot See Cost

questions.stem: On another fleet with one year's budget, a colleague sorts units by risk removed per $k and skips any unit that no longer fits. Compared with the 0-1 model, what does the page lead you to expect?

options.text: It matches the model, since greedy by ratio is exact on one budget
options.says: On the 500-unit fleet the model removed $109k more than the ratio ranking.

options.text: It removes less than worst-first, since it ignores condition scores
It removes more than the model, since skipping misfits uses all money
options.says: It left $160k unspent; the model's value equalled its bound.

options.text: It comes close, but gives no bound and cannot hold a second rule
options.says: Right: close on one budget, with nowhere to put the later rules.

origin.section: A Condition Score Is Not Risk, and the Ranking Cannot See Cost

questions.stem: A teammate's budget test checks only that a list spending exactly the budget is allowed. Why does the module's test also check a list just over the budget?

options.text: A model with no budget row allows the list at the limit as well
options.says: Right: only the refused list fails a model that has lost its row.

options.text: The skeleton's stub refuses lists over budget, so it must be beaten
The 500-unit fleet needs it, since small fleets miss these errors
options.says: The tests never use the 500-unit fleet; they use three to eight units.

options.text: HiGHS refuses a list at the limit, so the pair checks the solver
options.says: The test asserts that the list spending exactly $1,000k is allowed.

origin.section: The Tests Pin the Mistakes a Ranking Makes, on Fleets Small Enough to Check by Hand
